headline: Five Remain Missing After Nepal's Budhi Gandaki Flood
deck: Nepal's disaster authority said five people remain missing and 47 were rescued after a landslide-linked flood on the Budhi Gandaki in Gorkha.

flashpoint.note: NDRRMA says five remain missing after the Gorkha flood. House-loss figures still differ across reports.

body: Five people remain missing and 47 have been rescued after a landslide blocked the Budhi Gandaki River in Gorkha district, according to Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, Himalayan Times reported. [E7]
Himalayan Times said the missing people, two women and three men, were staying at a sheepfold in Ungiling, Chumchet. [E8]

The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority said the blockage triggered a large flood carrying mud and debris that swept away bridges, houses and infrastructure, Himalayan Times reported; Indian Express said a flash flood in the Budhi Gandaki River swept away several houses in Nepal's Gorkha district early on Sunday. [E7][E4]
Officials told people living along the river to move to higher ground, Indian Express reported. [E4]
Dharmendra Kumar Mishra, Gorkha's chief district officer, told Indian Express he got word of a major flood at 4:35 am on Sunday. [E4]
Residents along the Budhi Gandaki river in north central Nepal evacuated on Sunday as flash flooding destroyed homes and other structures in the area, AP reported. [E1]
Indian Express said the flood came down from Chumnubri Rural Municipality-6. [E5]
Mishra told Indian Express that early reports pointed to a landslide above Siuribas. [E5]
Nima Lama, the rural municipality chair, told Indian Express that the landslide blocked the Chumke Khola stream, and the flood followed. [E5]
Himalayan Times, citing the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority, and Lama, speaking to Indian Express, disagree on which watercourse the landslide blocked. [E7][E5]
Mishra said five to seven houses in the riverbed at Jagat were swept away, and a few more downstream may also have gone, Indian Express reported. [E5]
AP reported that the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority evacuated villagers and warned others to move to safer areas while remaining on alert until late Sunday. [E2]
At 6:40 am, Nepal's National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority sent an SMS alert from its Flood Forecasting Section, Indian Express reported. [E6]

Earlier Sunday, AP reported there were no immediate reports of casualties, and Indian Express said no deaths or injuries have been reported so far. [E3][E4] This paper's August files followed the Bhote Koshi–Trishuli cascade; Sunday's flood is a later event on the Budhi Gandaki.
